correctness.rationale: For S_mn the fully subdivided K_mn with all original m+n and mn midpoint vertices and shortest-path distances, reconstructed all six pairwise distance types (1,2,3,4), S_m×S_n orthogonal sectors, the exponential-kernel Bernstein argument forcing strict p-negativity of nonconstant sectors at 0<p<1, and the remaining two-dimensional quadratic form H(p) with entries K,J,R. Balanced J=0 gives p=log2(r/(r-1)) for r>=3, while at m=n=2 the graph C8 has p=1 and extra nullity. For unequal m,n, determinant changes from positive at 0 to negative at p_K and K<0; uniqueness follows strict-interior p-negative-type theorem, not merely numerically counting roots. Differentiating determinant at (p,h)=(0,0) gives the fixed-m coefficient (1+1/m)/[(4-1/m)log2-2log3]. Independently built adjacency BFS metrics and computed centered powered-distance eigenvalues and root H determinant for (2,2),(2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(3,4),(4,7); checked exact distance matrices and endpoint nullities including C8 three-dimensional equality space. No extrapolation from those finite tests.
residual_risks: The implicit root for unbalanced parts is not elementary; all-order proof relies on classical strict-interior negative type and the analytic decomposition, not finite spectra.
